entry.what: Expose ta_http_encode_post and ta_http_parse_request as two functions of the module (the POST of a BasicHTTP send, and the event of an incoming request), for an application's HTTP I/O processor and the adapter's W3C BasicHTTP loopback; p0-map names them.

entry.what: The event loop calls one turn function per environment (made at module init, referenced from the instance), with the Host as its argument and a second naming the handle (setImmediate(turn, host, 0), setTimeout(turn, ms, host, 1)), so scheduling makes no function and a pending handle holds the Host. The global timer functions are looked up at each call, so an application's fake timers apply. A delay is milliseconds rounded by double arithmetic and clamped to 2^31-1 (setTimeout fires at once beyond it); an early fire is an idle turn that arms the rest. The handles are strong napi_refs on the host, cleared and deleted at close; EXHAUSTED and FAULT schedule no next turn (the next input or idle() does), as Python's asyncio driver.
entry.why: Node-API callbacks need a function value; one per environment is the cheapest. Node and Bun both warn and use 1 ms for a delay over 2^31-1.
